question.text: Which of the following best describes the category membership distinction between Category-I and Category-II FPIs?

answer.text: Category-I FPIs are taxed at a higher rate than Category-II FPIs

Category-I covers government/government-related entities, pension/university funds, regulated entities and FATF-linked entities; Category-II covers regulated funds not eligible as Category-I, endowments/foundations, charities, corporate bodies, family offices, individuals, client-investing regulated entities and unregulated funds
Category-I FPIs can invest only in listed securities while Category-II can invest in unlisted securities
Category-I FPIs can invest only in equity while Category-II can invest in both equity and debt

explanation.text: The Logic: The Category-I/Category-II distinction is defined by the type of entity, not by tax rate or investment universe. Category-I includes government and government-related entities, pension and university funds, regulated entities and FATF-linked entities. Category-II is the residual bucket covering regulated funds not eligible as Category-I, endowments and foundations, charities, corporate bodies, family offices, individuals, regulated entities investing on behalf of clients, and unregulated funds. The Trap: Both categories may invest under the same underlying regulatory route - the answer choices that frame the distinction in terms of tax or asset-class eligibility misread the categorisation, which is about who the investor is. Note: When in doubt, anchor on entity type: if the candidate is government, regulated or FATF-linked, it sits in Category-I; otherwise it generally falls into Category-II.
